subject: Economics
description: World Bank, IMF, ADB, WTO, NDB — roles and structure

questions.stem: The World Bank's lending arm for middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries is the:

options.option_text: IBRD (International Bank for Reconstruction and Development)

questions.explanation: World Bank Group has 5 institutions: IBRD (middle-income / creditworthy low-income country lending, the largest arm), IDA (concessional loans / grants to the poorest countries), IFC (private-sector lending), MIGA (political-risk insurance), ICSID (investment dispute settlement). 'World Bank' narrowly = IBRD + IDA. HQ — Washington DC. President is traditionally an American nominee.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: India's largest shareholder position — after the 2023 quota reforms — in the IMF is approximately:
questions.explanation: India's IMF quota share is ~2.75 % (8th among member countries, after the US, Japan, China, Germany, UK, France, Italy). A country's quota determines its voting share, borrowing access, and SDR allocation. The IMF is headquartered in Washington DC; the MD is traditionally European. Kristalina Georgieva (Bulgaria) is the current MD. Gita Gopinath (Indian-American) served as Chief Economist 2019-22, now Deputy MD.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The 'New Development Bank' (NDB) is a multilateral development bank set up by:
questions.explanation: NDB (originally the BRICS Development Bank) — established 2015 by Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa. HQ in Shanghai; first President was K.V. Kamath of India (2015-20). Founding authorised capital of US$ 100 billion, equal shareholding. Funds infrastructure and sustainable-development projects in member and other emerging / developing countries. Intended as a complement / alternative to the Western-dominated IMF and World Bank.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has its headquarters in:
questions.explanation: ADB — founded 1966 — HQ in Manila, Philippines. Largest shareholders are Japan and the US (each ~15.6 %); India is a founding member. By convention, the ADB President has always been Japanese. A rival China-led institution is the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB, 2016) — HQ in Beijing, India is among its largest borrowers.

questions.stem: The WTO replaced which pre-existing trade body in 1995?
questions.explanation: GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, 1947) ran eight negotiation rounds. The Uruguay Round (1986-94) produced the Marrakesh Agreement establishing the WTO from 1 January 1995. WTO covers goods (GATT legacy), services (GATS), intellectual property (TRIPS), and has a dispute-settlement mechanism. India is a founding member. Current Director-General — Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The 'Bretton Woods Conference' of 1944 led to the creation of which two international financial institutions?
questions.explanation: Bretton Woods (July 1944) — 44 Allied nations met at the Mount Washington Hotel, New Hampshire, to plan the post-war economic order. It created the IMF (managing exchange rates, short-term payments crises) and the IBRD / World Bank (long-term development finance). Both began operations in 1945. The Bretton Woods 'fixed but adjustable' exchange-rate system (dollar pegged to gold, others pegged to dollar) broke down in 1971 when the US ended gold convertibility.

questions.stem: The IMF's Special Drawing Rights (SDR) is:

options.option_text: A reserve asset whose value is based on a basket of five currencies
A type of bond issued by the US Treasury

questions.explanation: SDR — created by the IMF in 1969 — is an international reserve asset that members hold in their reserves alongside gold and major currencies. Its value is set from a basket of five currencies — US dollar, Euro, Chinese Renminbi (added 2016), Japanese Yen, British Pound. Weights are reviewed every five years. Countries can use SDRs to settle IMF payments and swap them for hard currency with other members.
